rounds.text: Tridhya Tech Ltd is heavily discounted by the market, trading at a steep price-to-book ratio of just 0.54x against a book value of ₹ 19.1 while the stock price sits at a modest ₹ 10.4 [E2]. This valuation disconnect leaves the micro-cap company with a market capitalisation of only ₹ 24.3 Cr [E3] despite a robust 5-year compounded sales growth rate of 20% [E8]. Fundamental momentum has dramatically flipped toward recovery, highlighted by an extraordinary 132% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E13] that vastly outstrips the sector median profit growth of 12.9% [E64]. Furthermore, recent price-led dynamics show that profit growth exceeds 1-year price growth by 174%, indicating the business is beginning to outperform market expectations [E47]. Conceded: the 5-year compounded profit growth sits at -12% [E11], the 3-year compounded profit growth is down 43% [E12], and returns on capital remain low with a ROCE of 5.6% [E6] and an ROE of 1.0% [E7].

Tridhya Tech Ltd carries a deeply concerning fundamental profile, highlighted by an abysmal return on equity of 1.0% and an underwhelming ROCE of 5.6% [E6, E7]. This weak capital efficiency is compounded by severe historical profit contraction, with compounded profit growth plummeting by 12% over five years and accelerating downward to -43% over three years [E11, E12]. Furthermore, the business trades at an exorbitant P/E ratio of 52.9x, which stands in stark contrast to its negligible dividend yield of 0.00% and a recent sharp top-line contraction of 48% year-over-year [E1, E4, E58]. Although the stock sits low at 26% of its 52-week range and features a low price-to-book ratio of 0.54x, these metrics merely reflect the market's justified skepticism toward the company's deteriorating operational momentum [E2, E5]. However, these isolated bright spots are entirely undermined by decelerating earnings growth and screen flags for structural weakness [E59].

Conceded: [E1] and [E4]. The bear cites a P/E of 52.9x and a 0.00% dividend yield, but these figures must be weighed against a compelling price-to-book ratio of just 0.54x, meaning the stock trades at nearly half of its underlying book value of ₹ 19.1 per share [E2]. While the bear highlights weak returns on equity and capital [E6, E7] and past profit contraction [E11, E12], it completely ignores the dramatic operational turnaround where trailing twelve-month compounded profit growth has surged by 132% [E13]. This explosive recent earnings expansion far outpaces the sector median profit growth of 12.9% [E64].
